resolution: Added an 'all parts' toggle to the Studio object-mode toolbar (shows with 2+ parts) so the whole model resizes/moves/rotates as one. Before, the object gizmo only transformed the active layer about its OWN centroid — resizing layers one at a time scaled each toward a different center and broke the assembly (the user's 'fucks it all up'). With 'all' on, grabbing the gizmo (now anchored at the model's COMMON world centroid) transforms EVERY part together: move translates all by the same delta, per-axis + uniform resize scale all about the shared anchor, rotate spins all about the shared axis — proportions and relative placement hold. Implemented as a self-contained parallel to the single-part drag (multiGizmoDragRef + a multiDraft live preview that re-uses each part's own dyn slot, commits per part on release). No concave guard needed since a whole-model affine transform can't buckle a convex quad. Built clean; /model boots (self-shot PASS).
